questions.q: What is the Ports tab for?
questions.explain: Every UART is given a role; without it the FC does not know where to look for the receiver or GPS.

questions.q: Serial RX is enabled on UART2, and the receiver is soldered to UART1. The result?
options: Arming is impossible because of RXLOSS
The FC listens on the wrong port
The VTX cannot be set up
questions.explain: The port role must match the physical connection.

questions.q: Can two devices be assigned to one UART?
options: Only GPS and VTX on an F7
Only in the pairs the firmware allows
questions.explain: A UART is one TX/RX pair, and the firmware accepts only certain pairs of functions on one port: MSP with telemetry, Blackbox or VTX_MSP; Serial RX with some telemetry. Any other pair makes the port configuration invalid.
A software emulation of a UART on ordinary pins: it helps when the UARTs have run out, but it is not suitable for SBUS.

questions.q: The FC's USB port is shown in Ports as…
questions.explain: USB VCP is the virtual COM port for the configurator and the CLI.
Identifier 2 = UART3, 64 = Serial RX. This is the 4.5 notation; in 2025.12 `diff` writes `serial UART3 64 …`, but it accepts the numbers too.

questions.q: How many ports with MSP are allowed at the same time?
options: Any number, if the baud rates differ
questions.explain: A fourth makes the port configuration invalid, and at boot all ports are reset to the board defaults.

questions.q: An ExpressLRS receiver is connected to UART2. The aircraft does not see the sticks. The cause is in this diff:
questions.fragment:
serial 1 64 115200 57600 0 115200
set serialrx_provider = SBUS
set serialrx_inverted = OFF
options: serialrx_provider = SBUS, while ELRS speaks CRSF — serialrx_provider = CRSF is needed
Mask 64 on UART2 means MSP, not Serial RX — the receiver is connected to a telemetry port
115200 is too slow for ELRS: CRSF requires 420000, and that is set in the serial command
serialrx_inverted = OFF: ELRS on UART2 needs the software inverter enabled
questions.explain: serial 1 (UART2) with mask 64 is Serial RX, which is correct; the protocol is the wrong one.
